events.title: Shannon applies Boolean algebra to switching circuits
events.summary: Claude Shannon submitted his [MIT] master's thesis on August 10, 1937 — showing that [Boolean algebra] can systematically design [relay] and [switching circuits].
events.about: Shannon proved circuit design is [isomorphic] to logic: AND, OR, and NOT maps directly to switches and relays. Every digital chip, from 1940s [telephone exchange]s to modern [CPU]s, inherits this insight that hardware is executable [Boolean algebra].

narrative.whyChosen: This thesis is often called the most important master's thesis of the 20th century.
narrative.whyImportant: It turned circuit design from craft into symbolic manipulation — the ancestor of hardware description languages.
narrative.problemSolved: Engineers designed relay networks by trial and error with no unified mathematical method.
